title: Observability: hybrid export coordinator and ring-buffer logwriter refactor
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Scope: Replace several synchronous/alloc-heavy pieces in the observability path with a hybrid push-pull export coordinator, introduce a bounded ring-buffer logwriter for low-allocation log batching, and decouple metric combiner into a non-blocking worker. Goals: reduce p99 latency contribution from telemetry, lower CPU/temp spikes during ingestion bursts, and shrink tail memory usage from trace/span buffering. Includes OpenTelemetry SDK upgrade (+plugins) and adapter shim to preserve existing semantic conventions.

Outcomes/Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end telemetry p99 contribution reduced by >=30% on 99th percentile invocation latency in synthetic burst tests.
- Total CPU usage of agent/forwarder process reduced by >=20% on representative load profile.
- No >0.5% increase in dropped traces/metrics during 10x synthetic bursts.
- Backwards-compatible wire format to existing exporters; migration rollout plan that allows canary toggles per-region.

Implementation notes:
- Build an "export coordinator" that multiplexes exporters but uses pull-based sampling feedback to avoid head-of-line blocking when downstream exporters are slow. The coordinator exposes a bounded request queue per-exporter with backpressure signals for the serving runtime.
- Replace current sync log writer with a fixed-size ring buffer and background flusher; use preallocated slices to reduce GC churn; limit per-tenant buffer to avoid OOM from noisy tenants.
- Move metric aggregation into a lock-free combiner (per-shard) with periodic merge; add a low-memory path for sparse cardinality metrics.
- Upgrade OpenTelemetry SDK to 1.16.x and vendor only the tracer/metrics packages we use; add compatibility adapter for legacy span attributes used by downstream pipelines.
- Add feature flag runtime.telemetry.export.coordinator with three modes: off (current behavior), canary (new path for 10% of traffic), on (full traffic).

Rollout plan:
1) Merge feature branch behind flag; run integration tests and internal benchmarking.
2) Canary 10% in staging; run 48h synthetic burst test and compare trace/metric loss.
3) Canary 5% production in non-critical region; monitor dashboards for latency, drops, CPU.
4) Ramp to 50% then 100% over 24h windows if no regressions.

Monitoring & rollback:
- Dashboards: telemetry-forwarder-p99, telemetry-forwarder-cpu, tracing-dropped-rate, metrics-aggregation-lag.
- Rollback triggers: >10% regression on p50/p99 producer latency attributable to forwarder, >0.5% increase in dropped telemetry, or >15% sustained CPU regression.

Risks and mitigations:
- Upgrading OTEL may change attribute semantics: we will include an adapter shim and run a comparison pass in parallel to detect mismatches.
- Third-party exporter rate-limit behavior could expose hidden backpressure—we'll run per-exporter slow downstream simulations during canary.
- Memory usage spikes from ring buffer misconfiguration — buffer sizes are bounded per-tenant and configurable at startup.

Docs and artifacts:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/OBS-Modernization-Ringbuf+ExportCoordinator (design and perf notes)
- Benchmark results (internal): https://drive.redwood.com/observability/benchmarks/export-coordinator-2026-02-20.md
